title: Working at Redwood — Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits, Hiring & Onboarding, and Internal Tools
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Overview

This document is the single-source reference for employees about working at Redwood: company culture and expectations, role definitions and career ladders, benefits and perks, the hiring and new-hire onboarding process, and the set of internal tools you'll use day-to-day. It is maintained by People Ops; please send suggested edits to people-ops@redwood.example.

1) Working at Redwood — culture & expectations

Introduction
Redwood is an engineering-first company focused on production-grade inference. We value craftsmanship, ownership, and pragmatic iteration. Our core working principles are:
- Ship small, validate fast: prioritize measurable outcomes and early validation.
- Empathy and clarity: write clear docs, communicate assumptions, and foster psychological safety.
- Reliability-first: design for observability and graceful degradation.
- Customer-centricity: measure features against real customer impact and cost.

Ways of working
- Default to asynchronous communication: document decisions and use issues/PRs for design discussion.
- Synchronous meetings are for alignment, not status. Use short agendas and clear action items.
- Code reviews are required for all changes to shared services and infra. Follow the PR checklist in eng-developer-experience.

Hybrid/remote policy
- Redwood operates a flexible remote/hybrid model. Teams may set a weekly core in-office cadence for collaboration days; exceptions require manager approval.
- Office locations are available for team collaboration, and travel support is available for distributed teams during major launches. See travel policy for reimbursement details.

2) Roles & career ladders

Role families
Redwood maintains leveling guides for these families: Engineering (Backend, Runtime, SRE), Product (PM, TPM, Design), Applied ML & Research, Data & Analytics, DevRel/Developer Experience, Customer Success, Sales & GTM, People Ops, Finance & Legal, Security. Leveling docs live in the team wiki and are referenced below.

Level structure (example: Engineering)
- E1 / IC1: New graduate / early-career contributor. Focus: shipping small features, learning systems.
- E2 / IC2: Full contributor. Focus: owning features, reliable delivery, mentoring interns.
- E3 / IC3: Senior engineer. Focus: system design, cross-team delivery, technical direction.
- E4 / IC4: Staff engineer. Focus: technical strategy, large cross-functional initiatives, mentorship for senior engineers.
- E5 / IC5: Principal / distinguished. Focus: long-range architecture, organization-wide technical strategy.

Promotion criteria (high-level)
Promotions are based on demonstrated impact, scope, leadership (executional and technical), and consistent embodiment of company values. Typical evidence includes: project summaries, impact metrics (latency/cost improvements, uptime gains), peer feedback, and manager feedback. Formal promotion windows occur quarterly; exceptions for exceptional cases are handled ad hoc.

Career conversation cadence
- New hires: 30/60/90 day check-ins with manager and People Ops onboarding buddy.
- Ongoing: career calibration conversations twice a year as part of performance reviews; informal 1:1s monthly.

3) Benefits & perks

Summary (standard US offering — country variations apply)
- Health: medical, dental, and vision plans with company contribution.
- Financial: 401(k) with company match up to 4% after eligibility period; equity grants at hire and refreshers as part of compensation review.
- Time off: generous PTO policy (unlimited/manager-guided), 12 company holidays + company-wide shut down week in December. Parental leave: 16 weeks primary caregiver, 8 weeks secondary caregiver (paid).
- Family & wellness: fertility & family planning benefits, mental health EAP and 8 free therapy sessions per year.
- Learning & development: $2,000 L&D stipend per year, internal tech talks, and mentoring programs.
- Commuter & home office: stipend for home office setup up to $1,000 on hire; commuter benefits where applicable.
- Perks: monthly social stipend, team offsites budget, paid volunteer days.

Expenses & approvals
- File expenses via Expensely (internal expense tool). See the expense guide for allowed categories and receipt rules. Manager approval required for reimbursements.

4) Hiring process — overview for candidates and hiring managers

Goals
- Hire fast with high bar; ensure consistency and fairness; measure candidate experience.

Standard process (timeline: target 3–6 weeks)
1. Requisition and job posting: Manager creates JIRA requisition and coordinates with Recruiting.
2. Phone screen: 30–45 minute recruiter call to review background and logistics.
3. Technical/role interview loop: 3–4 interviews tailored to role family (take-home coding or design exercise as applicable).
4. Hiring committee review: cross-functional committee reviews feedback and ICs above E3.
5. Offer & negotiation: Recruiting and Hiring Manager coordinate comp and equity within comp band.
6. Background & reference checks: conducted after verbal offer.

Interview guidelines for interviewers
- Use standard evaluation rubrics; avoid illegal or biased questions.
- Provide actionable feedback within 48 hours and submit to the interview scheduler.
- Interview debriefs should document strengths, risks, and calibration notes.

Diversity & inclusion
- Redwood runs diverse sourcing programs and structured interview training for all interviewers. Reasonable accommodations are provided for candidates on request.

5) New-hire onboarding & 30/60/90 checklist

Before day 1
- Recruiting sends Welcome packet and new-hire form. People Ops provisions equipment request to IT.

Day 1–7 (week 0)
- Orientation session (People Ops): company mission, values, payroll, benefits enrollment.
- Manager kickoff: team goals, immediate priorities, 30/60/90 expectations.
- Access provisioning: GitHub, Google Workspace, Slack, internal wiki, repo permissions, VPN, and cloud console. See "Internal Tools & Access" below for exact access steps.

First 30 days
- Complete onboarding learning path on LearnRedwood (required: security awareness, code of conduct, handling customer data).
- Deliver a small onboarding project and demo to the team.
- Weekly 1:1s with manager and onboarding buddy.

30–90 days
- Expand scope: own a low-risk production task (bug fix, minor feature) to learn CI/CD and deployment process.
- Career conversation at day 90 and leveling calibration if relevant.

Onboarding checklist (short)
- [ ] Equipment received and tested (laptop, peripherals)
- [ ] Accounts and repo access confirmed
- [ ] Completed security & compliance training
- [ ] Completed first onboarding project and demo
- [ ] Set up 1:1s and recurring team rituals

6) Internal tools & access (quick reference)

Primary tools and owners
- Slack — company communication. Owner: People Ops. Channel guidelines: use #team-* and #project-* for work topics; keep #general for announcements.
- GitHub — source control. Owner: Eng Developer Experience. Repos follow naming conventions: redwood/* for services, redwood-infra/* for infra.
- LearnRedwood (LMS) — onboarding courses, required compliance training. Owner: People Ops.
- JIRA — work tracking and hiring requisitions. Owner: Eng Platform. Use team boards for sprint planning; follow issue templates.
- Expensely — expense submissions and approvals. Owner: Finance.
- Vaulted — secrets and KMS onboarding (for private deployments). Owner: Security. Request via security-requests@redwood.example.
- Console & Datadog — observability and dashboards. Owner: Eng Platform. Access granted after manager sign-off and SRE onboarding.
- Employee directory & SSO — single sign-on through Okta. Owner: IT.

Access request flow
1. New hire submits access form (People Ops initiates for hires).
2. Manager approves required tools and confirms role-based access list (RBAC).
3. IT provisions accounts; security performs role-based checks for sensitive resources.
4. Owner teams grant repo/service-level permissions.

Secrets & sensitive data handling
- Do not store secrets in plain text, Slack, or public repos. Use Vaulted for secret distribution. All engineers must complete secrets management training in LearnRedwood within first 14 days.

7) Performance management & compensation cadence

Performance cycles
- Annual performance review with semi-annual calibration. Objectives are documented in JIRA/OKR tracked per team.
- Managers provide continuous feedback; formal written feedback occurs at mid-year and year-end cycles.

Compensation reviews
- Compensation is reviewed annually; role level or promotion reviews may include off-cycle adjustments for retention or market movement. Equity refresh decisions are discretionary and communicated during comp review.

8) FAQs & common scenarios

Q: Who do I ask about visa sponsorship?
A: People Ops handles immigration and visa sponsorship. Email people-ops@redwood.example; your recruiter will also coordinate.

Q: How do I request parental leave?
A: Submit a parental leave request via the HR portal and talk with People Ops for timing and benefits specifics.

Q: How do I escalate an access issue to production systems?
A: Contact SRE on-call via #oncall Slack channel and follow the runbook in eng-sre/runbooks. For urgent access, open a P0 ticket with Security.
